prompt: Which two things do the families of chart tools trade against each other?

choices.text: Price and the colours available
choices.why: Colours are available everywhere.

choices.text: Honesty and accuracy of the result
choices.why: Every tool can draw honestly; that depends on you.

choices.text: Screen size and file size
choices.why: Neither decides the choice.

choices.text: First-chart speed against control
choices.why: Right. No tool is best at both.

prompt: Which question does the lesson say people forget when choosing a tool?

choices.text: Does it support the newest chart types?
choices.why: The course's charts are all old and well understood.

choices.text: Who will maintain it when you leave?
choices.why: Right. A dashboard nobody else can open stops being updated.

choices.text: Is it the one used by the biggest companies?
choices.why: Popularity elsewhere does not maintain your dashboard.

choices.text: Can it draw in 3D?
choices.why: Lesson 16 says not to.

prompt: Many people will open a dashboard every week and want to filter it. Which family fits best?

choices.text: A spreadsheet emailed around every Monday
choices.why: Copies drift apart and cannot be filtered together.

choices.text: A BI tool
choices.why: Right: interaction, refresh and permissions.

choices.text: A static PNG made with a plotting library
choices.why: A PNG cannot be filtered.

choices.text: A hand-drawn chart photographed for the intranet
choices.why: Nothing there updates.

prompt: What changes from one tool to another, according to the lesson?

choices.text: Where rules are set, and defaults
choices.why: Right. The rules themselves stay the same.

choices.text: Whether bars need to start at zero
choices.why: That holds in every tool.

choices.text: Whether a title should make a claim
choices.why: That holds in every tool.

choices.text: How much contrast text needs
choices.why: WCAG does not depend on the tool.

prompt: A spreadsheet bar chart shows the regions in the order the rows were typed. What is the fix?

choices.text: Pick the 3D version of the chart instead
choices.why: Depth does not sort anything.

choices.text: Add a legend that explains the order
choices.why: A legend cannot sort bars.

choices.text: Sort the data before charting it
choices.why: Right. The chart follows the rows.

choices.text: Give each bar a different colour
choices.why: Colour does not change the order.

prompt: What do spreadsheets do least well, of these?

choices.text: Drawing a quick chart from a table
choices.why: That is what they do best.

choices.text: Showing data that is already in a grid
choices.why: That is their starting point.

choices.text: Letting you change a chart's title
choices.why: Every spreadsheet does that.

choices.text: Repeating the same chart next month
choices.why: Right. The steps are repeated from memory.

prompt: Why can adding a series to a spreadsheet chart recolour the others?

choices.text: Spreadsheets run out of colours after three
choices.why: They have plenty.

choices.text: The new series always takes the brightest colour
choices.why: Position, not brightness, decides.

choices.text: Colours are assigned by position
choices.why: Right, so a colour's meaning can move (lesson 13).

choices.text: The chart switches to a 3D style
choices.why: Adding a series does not change the style.

prompt: What happens to a workbook saved from Tableau's free edition?

choices.text: It goes public, with its data open to download
choices.why: Right. Tableau Public is a public gallery.

choices.text: It is kept on your own computer only
choices.why: The free edition saves to Tableau Public.

choices.text: It is shared with your company's server
choices.why: That needs a paid product.

choices.text: It expires after thirty days
choices.why: It stays, and stays public.

prompt: A BI tool picks a chart type for the fields you dragged in. What should you do?

choices.text: Accept it: the tool has seen the data
choices.why: Seeing the data is not knowing the question.

choices.text: Switch it to a pie chart for dashboards
choices.why: Pies are rarely the best choice.

choices.text: Add every remaining field to it
choices.why: That makes it worse.

choices.text: Treat it as a guess and check it
choices.why: Right, against lesson 2's ranking.

prompt: What does a BI tool give that is hard to build with a plotting library?

choices.text: Bars that start at zero by default
choices.why: Libraries do that too.

choices.text: Clicking one chart filters every other chart
choices.why: Right. Interaction comes built in.

choices.text: More accurate numbers in the chart
choices.why: Accuracy comes from the data.

choices.text: A wider choice of colour palettes
choices.why: Libraries have plenty.

prompt: Which of these should not go on a public gallery such as Tableau Public without permission? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Brazil's published census population by state
choices.why: That is already public.

choices.text: Your company's sales figures
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: Delivery times per driver
choices.why: Right. Each row is about a person.

choices.text: The invented Horta data from this course
choices.why: It describes nobody.

choices.text: A list of customers with their cities
choices.why: Right. That is personal data.

prompt: Match each library to what it is known for.

pairs.right: statistical charts on top of matplotlib
charts in layers, from the Grammar of Graphics
drawing anything in the browser from scratch

prompt: How do ggplot2 and Altair differ in style from matplotlib?

choices.text: They produce only interactive charts
choices.why: Both produce static charts too.

choices.text: They run only inside a spreadsheet
choices.why: They are code libraries.

choices.text: They need no data file
choices.why: Every chart needs data.

choices.text: You say what the chart is, and it works out the drawing
choices.why: Right. matplotlib asks how to draw each part.

prompt: What is the first thing code gives you that a chart made by clicking does not?

choices.text: A faster first chart than any spreadsheet
choices.why: The first chart is slower in code.

choices.text: Interaction without any extra work
choices.why: Interaction is work in a library.

choices.text: Charts that need no maintaining
choices.why: Somebody still has to maintain it.

choices.text: The steps are written down
choices.why: Right. Read, questioned and run again.

prompt: Why did plain.py produce a different file fingerprint each time?

choices.text: The data file changed between the two runs
choices.why: Nothing touched monthly.csv.

choices.text: The file holds the date and random ids
choices.why: Right. The picture is the same; the file is not.

choices.text: sha256sum gives a new answer every time
choices.why: The same file always gives the same fingerprint.

choices.text: matplotlib shuffles the order of the bars
choices.why: The bars are sorted the same way each run.

prompt: The matplotlib setting that gives the identifiers inside an SVG a fixed seed is svg.___.
After the two settings, the fingerprint of chart.svg changes one day. What does that mean?

choices.text: The data, the code or the library changed
choices.why: Right. A change in the file is now a real change.

choices.text: The date was written into the file again
choices.why: The setting removed it.

choices.text: The random identifiers came back
choices.why: The seed fixes them.

choices.text: Nothing; fingerprints drift over time
choices.why: A fingerprint of the same bytes never drifts.

prompt: Order the families of tools from the fastest first chart to the slowest, as the lesson places them.
This is the window of a drag-and-drop chart tool. Find each part.

labels.text: where the data's fields are listed
where the chart's look is set

hint: The filter is the funnel shape at the top.

prompt: You need one chart, today, from a table already in a spreadsheet, and nobody will need it again. What does the lesson suggest?

choices.text: Build a BI dashboard with a scheduled refresh
choices.why: A refresh for a chart nobody reopens is wasted work.

choices.text: Make it in the spreadsheet, fixing the defaults
choices.why: Right. It is the right tool for a one-off.

choices.text: Write it in D3.js for complete control
choices.why: Far slower than the job needs.

choices.text: Draw it by hand and scan it
choices.why: Not reproducible, and no faster.

prompt: Which statement sums up the lesson's view of tools?

choices.text: The best tool makes the course's rules unnecessary
choices.why: No tool knows your reader.

choices.text: Code is better than any other tool for every chart
choices.why: Spreadsheets and BI tools win in their own cases.

choices.text: Choose the tool with the most chart types
choices.why: The number of chart types is not the question.

choices.text: The defaults differ; the list of fixes does not
choices.why: Right. Every rule in the course is a setting somewhere.
